_description:
E-048 ARM B: the ~70M FSQ WINDOW codec at WIDTH 6 STRIDE 3 — 6 pentads (30 days) in, one embedding out, advance 15 days, OVERLAPPING. Chris, 2026-08-24: 'One embedding every 15 days (6 pentads/30 days as input, OVERLAPPING windows), advance by 15 days — each embedding has Argo as part of it, two consecutive ones share the same monthly Argo values.' That last clause is the mechanism: RG-Argo is a MONTHLY product written into one pentad bin per month (n_rg_live 252/3142 = 8.02%, the mid-month stamp), so a 30-day window always contains one Argo stamp while a 15-day ADVANCE gives the head twice the temporal resolution — and the price is that two consecutive embeddings share that stamp and half their input. MEASURED PARAMS 71,335,697 (71.336M), identical to arm A field for field: the stride changes the AXIS, not the model. 

THE PERSISTENCE BASELINE MOVES, AND THE METRIC DOES NOT. At stride 3 the previous embedding shares 3 of its 6 bins with the target, so 'predict the next embedding' is a strictly easier question than it is at stride 6 and persistence is stronger BY CONSTRUCTION. A one-step z-MSE ratio from this arm is comparable with another 15-day roll and with NOTHING ELSE — not with arm A, not with E-047a's month blocks, not with the pentad archive. The axis says so at startup (ml/timeblocks.py:BlockAxis.describe), the roll's artefact carries `blocks.persistence_note` beside the numbers, and ml/plans/E048_fsq_block_sweep.md pre-registers which comparisons are legal. What IS comparable across the two arms: the head's skill at a FIXED HORIZON IN DAYS (the day-defined bands and day-matched leads are derived from the stride — h1-6 at 15 d covers the same 90 days as h1-3 at 30 d), the reconstruction audit, and the probe. 

Everything else is arm A's, unchanged: fsq_levels '8' with fsq_ladder 'auto' (the lattice fitted per z-dimension at step 2,000 and recorded in the checkpoint), 768x10 with 8 heads (head_dim 96), d_dec 512, d_z 64, patch 1, anomaly, holdout_lon '0,0', head_probe true, batch 512. DISPATCH WITH `resume` EMPTY: a fresh codec. 

ONE COST DIFFERENCE WORTH KNOWING BEFORE DISPATCH: this arm's Z has TWICE the rows of arm A's over the same record (2x the blocks), so the stage-2 embed pass and every stencil the head reads are 2x, while the codec's own training cost per STEP is identical — the blocks are the sampling pool, not the step budget.
_provenance:
Copied field for field from ml/recipes/f4r2-70M-fsqblock-w6s6.json (E-048 arm A) changing exactly one key: time_block '6/6' -> '6/3'. That is the whole design of the pair — one variable, the STRIDE, against a shared codec geometry, a shared bottleneck and a shared tensor — and it is what makes 'does an overlapping window buy anything' answerable in one wave. Arm A's own provenance carries the lineage back to ml/recipes/f4r2-40M-monthblock-b512.json (E-047a-fast) and the batch arithmetic on the TPU v5e; both apply here unchanged, because the stride does not touch the per-step shapes: a step still encodes `batch` windows of 6x40+2 = 242 tokens. 

NOTHING HAS BEEN RUN AT THIS CONFIGURATION. ml/CLAUDE.md 3b's harder clause applies in full — new codec, new cadence, new bottleneck, and on top of that a cadence at which NO replicate pair has ever been measured (the pentad forecast-ratio pair #427/#432 is the only non-monthly pair in the record, at |Δ| 0.00113, and it is not this cadence). The first result off this recipe buys its own replication before any number from it is written as a level rather than a first reading.
